svg.title: GLD period optimization — in-sample ceilings, no selectable candidate
svg.text: GLD period optimizer: in-sample ceilings, NO selectable candidate (Plan 20 close-out)
dense, ~45% flat, NOT selected: no candidate at either horizon cleared the frozen 70.0% time-in-market floor, so best is None for medium, long and combined
CEILING: every metric here is an IN-SAMPLE CEILING on the same history the periods were fit on. The oracle buys the whole book all-in on every pinned buy date and sells
all-out on every pinned sell date, so it measures PERIOD QUALITY, never achievable performance — real DCA drips and cannot buy one close. Only the split-sample read
(fit on the first half, score on the unseen second half) says anything out-of-sample-ish, and both sides must be read next to this sentence.
frozen objective: maximize oracle Sharpe, tie-break Calmar, then CAGR, subject to a time-in-market floor of 70.0% of days (period_optimize.EXPOSURE_FLOOR_PCT /
risk-adjusted conventions (sdca/risk_metrics.py): simple per-day returns, annualization 252, risk-free 0, drawdown reused from walk_forward..
A. GLD close and the pivot pins behind the period sets (820 combined windows = pm60 + pm180)

Every tick is a pivot the price series produced: the oracle sells flat at a peak pin and buys at a trough pin, so dense pins buy the flat time. Medium finds one pin every ~17 bars (pivot widths are counted in bars); 1 window exit is truncated at the last bar (medium_trough_20260916_pm60).
B. Time in market (oracle exposure) — every candidate misses the floor
Exposure barely moves across the search width (< 1.5 pp spread per horizon): pivot DENSITY, not the candidate width, decides how much time is flat, and density is
asset-independent. Each horizon is its OWN grid — never a cross-grid contest.
frozen floor 70.0% (every candidate is left of it)

Flat share is the complement: the rank-1 medium set is 45.26% flat (exposure 54.74%), the combined set 48.66% (51.34%). Both comparators are invested from day 0, so 100.00% is a property of those two paths.
C. Oracle Sharpe — even the diagnostic ceilings LOSE to buy-and-hold
In-sample ceilings on the same history the periods were fit on: they measure PERIOD QUALITY, never achievable performance. Every candidate row above is a rank-1 row that
FAILED the floor, never a selection.
Sharpe alone is not the whole read: the period sets buy lower drawdown (combined 31.57% vs lump 45.56%) at about half the exposure (panel B).
dense, ~45% flat, NOT selected: no candidate at either horizon cleared the frozen 70.0% time-in-market floor, so best is None for medium, long and combined.
